usage: Replay the owner question alone in a fresh native chat. Keep the expectation and reference links on the reviewer side. These cases become known regressions after publication. Use a new question to test transfer.

cases.owner_question: One long-running standalone Docker worker on a compute Spark has --restart=on-failure:3. It sometimes exits cleanly to recycle. We need it to restart after that and after a Docker daemon restart, but an operator's deliberate stop for maintenance must survive even a daemon restart. Which restart policy should we put in the launcher, and would always be equivalent?
cases.reviewer_expectation: Pick the restart policy that respects an intentional stop.

cases.owner_question: Our Java 21 service publishes a manifest with Files.move(tmp, current, ATOMIC_MOVE, REPLACE_EXISTING). current already exists and readers must always see a complete old or new manifest. tmp is created beside current, but we support several filesystem providers. Does that call guarantee replacement on every provider, and what should we do if the provider refuses it?
cases.reviewer_expectation: Leave the current publication in place if its replacement cannot meet the reader guarantee.

cases.owner_question: A partner's incident note says their worker received a fresh message from their private Amazon SQS standard queue at 09:00:00, then crashed at 09:00:08 without deleting it. The consumer uses the queue's visibility setting and never extends it. Can another worker process the message again, and what exact time is their queue configured to make it visible again?
cases.reviewer_expectation: Explain possible redelivery, mark the configured private timeout unknown and identify the queue attribute to read.

cases.owner_question: We have to return an archive disk tonight. Our restic 0.18.0 backup printed a new snapshot ID but exited with status 3. A colleague then ran restic check --read-data and it passed. We promised every file from this disk would be recoverable before we erase it. Can we sign off and wipe it now? If not, what would let us sign off?
cases.reviewer_expectation: Retain the only source until recoverability of every intended file can be verified. Check integrity and source completeness separately.

cases.owner_question: Our production Python diagnostic printed logging.getLogger("jobs.reader").level as 0 (NOTSET). Does that turn logging off for this logger, and what exact effective level is it using right now?
cases.reviewer_expectation: Explain what the observed local level means; identify the in-process measurement that reveals the actual effective level.

cases.owner_question:
We promise customers that none of their card funds will be reserved before a manager approves an order. Our proposed checkout confirms a live manual-capture PaymentIntent immediately; if the manager rejects the order, a webhook cancels it and logs the cancellation. Does this meet the promise? Where should the approval check go?

Our Stripe integration notes quote the processor:
“When you create a payment, you can place a hold on an eligible payment method to reserve funds that you can capture later.”
“This parameter instructs Stripe to authorize the amount but not capture it on the customer’s payment method.”
“If you need to cancel an authorization, you can cancel the PaymentIntent.”
cases.reviewer_expectation: Manager approval must precede the operation that can reserve funds. Later cancellation or a log cannot honor a promise that no hold ever existed.
